title: Hosted API inventoryized COGS and margin hedge scenarios
file_description: Exploratory spreadsheet that inventory-izes Hosted API direct and amortized COGS by model family and region, simulates margin outcomes under reserve / burst mixes, and surface margin-hedging recommendations tied to cache and model-substitution policies.
summary: This sheet synthesizes a per-token cost inventory across compute, amortized infra, licensing, and ops overhead; runs multi-factor sensitivity sweeps (cache hit rate, reserved capacity %, average sequence length, latency SLI requirement) and proposes concrete hedges (cache prioritization rules, reserve carveouts, model-substitution ladder). The goal is an operational playbook with actionable knobs to protect gross margin in regional and latency-constrained workloads.
assumptions: GPU hourly rates: region-specific inputs on Inventory tab
Sequence length distribution: 95th pctl = 512 tokens for chat-style workloads
KV cache hit calculation: prefix-only + session-KV conservative estimate
Amortization window: 12 months for GPUs and 36 months for infra licenses
Ops overhead: 8% of direct compute costs
sensitivity_scenarios: Base: current mix and cache 12% hit
Optimistic cache: +20% absolute hit -> reduces per-token compute by cached prefix fraction
Reserve-heavy: 60% reserved capacity, 40% burst -> lower unit compute but risk of wasted amortization if utilization < 70%
Spot-mix: 30% spot on non-latency paths -> 12-18% cost savings but higher preemption delta costs
Latency-strict: SLI tightened to p99<300ms forcing higher-cost models or smaller batch sizes
model_portfolio_notes: Family grouping: small (7B), medium (13B), large (70B+), embeddings separate SKU
Substitution ladder: large->medium->small for non-SLI requests; embeddings offload to specialized infra
Quantization options: int8/4Q suggested for medium/large where quality delta acceptable
simulation_findings: Cache hit increases from 12% -> 32% reduces amortized_ppk by 14-22% depending on model family
Reserving 50-70% capacity yields 8-12% ppk improvement if utilization > 75%; below 60% utilization the amortization loss dominates
Latency SLI tightening forces a 6-9% ppk increase due to smaller batch sizes and reduced batching efficiency
Model substitution for 18% of calls (non-critical) yields ~9% margin lift and 4% lower p99 under mixed workloads
recommendations: Immediate: prioritize prefix cache for session-heavy customers using the high-value model families (config rule + short TTL tuning)
Near-term (Q1): pilot a reserve carveout for mid-tier customers with target utilization SLAs and revenue-backed commits (start with 30% of pool)
Product: expose a model-substitution policy in API routes (opt-in) with per-route guardrails and safety thresholds
Infra: add a spot vs reserved optimizer in provisioning that simulates cost volatility monthly and adjusts spot percentage per region
Ops: run weekly margin telemetry for top 10 customers and trigger reserve reallocation if utilization drift > 10%
action_roadmap: Week 0-2: instrument inventory spreadsheet with hourly region cost feeds and sample customer traffic profiles
Week 3-6: run Monte Carlo sim across cache, reserve %, and seq length; produce heatmaps and cliff points
Q1: launch 3-week reserve pilot with 2 customers in us-west and eu-west
Q2: roll out model-substitution policy as beta flag in hosted API with telemetry collection
open_questions: What contract language and billing flows are needed for reserve carveouts? (finance/legal input)
How to surface substitution quality deltas to customers for opt-in? (DX + docs)
Is there appetite for a per-customer cache tier (paid) vs global TTL tuning?
